title: Terraform module: EKS provisioner with rolling-upgrade guard and health probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (redwood_private_eks_provisioner) that provisions EKS clusters for Redwood Private with built-in rolling-upgrade guard, health probes for control plane and node groups, and safe upgrade primitives. The module should support both managed and self-managed nodegroups, integrate with KMS cross-account keys, emit health metrics to CloudWatch, and wire-in automated pre/post upgrade hooks so higher-level orchestration (console / provisioner) can make rollout decisions atomically.
acceptance_criteria: Module can create a basic EKS cluster and nodegroups reproducibly from TF plan/apply
Upgrade flow: performing a minor/patch control plane or nodegroup upgrade uses the rolling-upgrade guard to verify node draining and pod reschedules before considering step successful

Health checks: control plane API reachability, kube-scheduler/etcd (managed control plane proxies), and node kubelet heartbeat metrics are emitted to CloudWatch with tags redwood:cluster and redwood:env
KMS: module accepts cross-account KMS alias/ARN and configures encryption for secrets and EBS volumes where applicable
Zero-downtime config: cluster-level config exposes parameters for maxUnavailable and parallelism for nodegroup rotations
Idempotency: re-applying TF plan does not cause destructive changes when no drift
Observability: module creates CloudWatch dashboards (optional) and exposes Prometheus metrics for upgrade guard progress via AWS Managed Prometheus metrics exporter
Integration tests: automated terraform/integration tests run in CI and pass in the smoke test matrix for 1.23, 1.24, and 1.25 Kubernetes versions
design_notes: We choose a single module that composes smaller submodules: networking (VPC+subnets), iam (roles/policies), eks-cluster (eks module wrapper), nodegroups (managed/self-managed), and guard-hooks (lambda/state-machine). The top-level module wires them together.

Rolling-upgrade guard: implemented as an optional Step Functions state machine + Lambda (invoked via terraform null_resource/local-exec) that validates node drain success by checking PodDisruptionBudgets, Pod readiness, and a configurable app-level probe URL (if provided). The guard emits success/failure to a CloudWatch metric namespace 'Redwood/Provisioner/UpgradeGuard'.

Health probes: control plane probe will call the EKS DescribeCluster endpoint and then perform a lightweight kubectl get --raw /healthz via the bastion or eksctl-proxy runner. Node health uses CloudWatch agent metrics (kubelet heartbeat) and Node status via the Kubernetes API.

Locking & concurrency: Terraform apply will acquire a DynamoDB state lock (existing pattern). For upgrade operations, the module can optionally create a SSM parameter acting as an operation lock so downstream orchestrators can detect in-flight upgrades.

Secrets & KMS: module accepts a kms_key_arn (string). If cross-account, it will configure iam::sts AssumeRole permissions passed as variables to the provisioner-runner. Do not auto-create cross-account keys.

Upgrade path: for managed control plane version bumps, we rely on EKS managed upgrade semantics; the module exposes pre_upgrade and post_upgrade Lambda hooks that are invoked by the provisioner operator to gate changes.
Backward compatibility: we will provide input variables mirroring previous provisioner module names but default new sensible values to encourage migration. Deprecate old module after one cycle.

Testing: include terratest suites for create/destroy and upgrade scenarios using small instance types to reduce cost. CI should mark test clusters with tag redwood:ci=true and auto-delete on failure or success.
migration_plan: Provide a migration recipe in the module README for teams using the legacy eks-provisioner module: 1) add module with dry-run flags and review plan; 2) set create_nodegroups = false and import existing nodegroups via terraform import; 3) flip to manage them and run small-scale upgrade canary; 4) validate metrics and rollback hooks; 5) apply to remaining clusters incrementally.
qa_plan: Unit-style TF fmt & validate checks in pre-commit
Terratest CI: create->upgrade->drain->destroy workflow for 3 Kubernetes versions
Chaos test: intentionally fail a single node drain and validate guard halts the upgrade with clear failure metric
Load smoke: spin up small synthetic workload and verify no request loss during nodegroup rotation under our maxUnavailable defaults
rollout_plan: Stage 1: merge module as experimental & publish provider registry artifact to internal registry
Stage 2: onboard one non-critical internal cluster (dev) and run full upgrade exercises
Stage 3: onboard staging clusters and verify CloudWatch dashboards and metrics
Stage 4: enable for production clusters behind a feature flag; require a two-person signoff for first 3 production upgrades
Stage 5: deprecate legacy module after two successful production rotations
risks: Terraform-driven invocation of Lambdas/StepFunctions adds operational surface area and IAM complexity
Misconfigured PodDisruptionBudgets or missing app-level probes can make the guard overly conservative leading to blocked upgrades
Cross-account KMS setups vary significantly between customers—automating too much may introduce security exposure
Cost: testing multiple K8s versions in CI increases spend unless we aggressively re-use test accounts and small instance types
